platforms.evidence: Native rooted replacement and recovery qualification

invariants.statement: Invalid or unauthorised requests never reach filesystem mutation
invariants.falsifier: Observe target mutation for a rejected request
invariants.residual_uncertainty: Administrator and Celestia account remain trusted

invariants.statement: Commit replaces only the configured-root target whose current digest matches the admitted precondition
invariants.falsifier: Replace an out-of-root, linked, reparse or changed target
invariants.residual_uncertainty: Filesystem and kernel correctness are assumed

invariants.statement: Verified is assigned only from an independent post-commit target observation
invariants.falsifier: Return verified when the observed target differs or is unavailable

invariants.statement: Recovery never repeats a rename whose commitment is uncertain
invariants.falsifier: Observe recovery performing a second replacement
invariants.residual_uncertainty: Power-loss semantics depend on the qualified filesystem

success_semantics: Verified means a rooted atomic replacement committed, a new target handle matched the replacement digest and terminal evidence became durable
refusal_semantics: Rejected requests perform no replacement and retain no replacement bytes
failure_semantics: Failed means evidence establishes that the target replacement did not occur
cancellation_semantics: Cancellation is terminal only before commitment; after commitment starts the result is verified or indeterminate
indeterminate_semantics: A possibly committed effect without a verified postcondition or required durable evidence is indeterminate
recovery_semantics: Recovery never repeats the effect; it reconciles retained intent against a new target observation
compatibility_or_reset_policy: No pre-release persistence compatibility is promised and superseded unused formats are deleted coherently
falsifiers: An out-of-root, linked, reparse or changed target is replaced
Cancellation after commitment is reported as no effect
Write-path bytes are accepted as independent verification
Cleanup failure overwrites the primary outcome
Unsupported platforms access a configured root
residual_limitations: Windows AMD64 on a qualified fixed local volume is the only supported execution boundary
Administrator and code running as the Celestia account can rewrite target and evidence files
Synchronous filesystem calls cannot be pre-empted safely
The manifest bounds schema represents the absence of a worker with zero process and worker time
non_goals: Dynamic discovery, plug-ins, generic operation interfaces or catalogues
Shared abstractions extracted before two operations prove identical ownership
Nested targets, file creation, directories, alternate data streams or network filesystems
Compatibility readers or migrations for unused pre-release formats
deletion_criteria: Delete the operation if rooted atomic replacement cannot be qualified on Windows AMD64
Delete the operation if recovery cannot distinguish verified from indeterminate without repeating an effect
Delete any shared abstraction introduced before a second proven owner requires it
